summary: Implemented a first Phase 1 AutoGrid and refinement planning surface with typed public models, concrete resolution behavior, IR lowering, docs, examples, and passing validation tests.
key_findings: `src/autofdtd/grid/specs.py` now includes `AutoGrid`, `GridRefinement`, and `LayerRefinementSpec`, and `GridSpec` can resolve wavelength-driven AutoGrid axes with axis-aligned layer refinement and a simple `max_scale` grading pass.
`src/autofdtd/ir/models.py` now carries typed `AutoGridIR`, `GridRefinementIR`, and `LayerRefinementSpecIR`, and `GridSpecIR` preserves refinement metadata alongside resolved grid geometry.

Validation and planning metadata were updated so `AutoGrid` and refinement specs are accepted, `GridSpec.wavelength` is required for AutoGrid axes, and `QuasiUniformGrid` remains an explicit deferred error.
Coverage was added for AutoGrid spacing, layer snapping/refinement behavior, container normalization, and IR lowering; `pytest tests/test_containers.py tests/test_grid.py tests/test_ir.py` passes.

artifacts.description: Public grid models and concrete AutoGrid/refinement resolution logic.
Typed IR lowering for AutoGrid, GridRefinement, LayerRefinementSpec, and extended GridSpecIR.
Updated grid normalization policy to accept implemented AutoGrid/refinement types and reject deferred QuasiUniformGrid explicitly.
Grid documentation updated with AutoGrid usage, refinement examples, and explicit Phase 1 limitations.
Example AutoGrid configuration with layer refinement metadata.
Grid behavior tests for AutoGrid spacing, refinement, and wavelength requirements.
Container normalization tests for AutoGrid/refinement acceptance and deferred QuasiUniformGrid rejection.
IR tests for AutoGrid and layer-refinement metadata lowering.
Condensed task handoff notes for later grid/compiler work.

follow_up_notes: Current AutoGrid scope is intentionally narrow: it is vacuum-baseline, axis-local, and only consumes axis-aligned `LayerRefinementSpec` body/bounds hints. Geometry-aware corner finding, snapping-point localization, and scene-driven meshing remain for later compiler work.
